title: Assemble the Day-One Package
subtitle: The readiness certificate, by lookup only
scenario: It is SD-1, 5:00 PM - the evening before the start. Here is the payoff: every fact the certificate needs already exists in an artifact you built. Fill each slot by LOOKING IT UP from the shelf on your left. If you find yourself retyping a status from memory, stop - the tracker already has it.
input: Assembly rule: every slot value must come from a stored artifact. The hire name and role are in onboarding-record.json. The four task states are in task-tracker.json (all done). The readiness line comes from readiness-gate.json (Day-One Ready). The start date is SD.
instructions: Open each artifact on the shelf as you need it - do not work from memory.
Fill the header slots from the onboarding record (hire name, role, start date).
Fill the four provisioning slots from the task tracker (all done).
Fill readiness from the gate, then validate to render day-one-package.md.

sections.title: Everything already exists
sections.body: You are not producing new facts here - you are assembling proven ones. The hire's details, the four task states, and the readiness call all live in artifacts you built. Assembly is lookup, not recall.

sections.title: Traceable by construction
sections.body: Because every slot is filled from a stored artifact, the certificate is auditable: each line points back to the record that justifies it. That is what makes the hiring manager able to trust it at a glance.

sections.title: The evening before
sections.body: The package is assembled on SD-1, the evening before the start. A hire who is ready the night before walks in Monday to a working laptop, live accounts, and a badge - not a scramble.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: day-one-package.md - the module's deliverable. It is handed to the hiring manager next and archived after.
